content.text:
I ran `npm test` (`node --test`): 10 tests, 7 pass, 3 fail. All three failures are bugs in the service code, not in the tests. I didn't change any files.

### 1. `findByEmail ignores soft-deleted users` (`tests/auth-service.test.js`)
`findByEmail` in `src/services/auth-service.js:5` searches users by email only, with the predicate `u.email === email`. It never checks `deleted_at`. So a lookup for `alan@example.com`, whose `deleted_at` is `'2026-01-04'`, returns Alan's record instead of `null`. Every other service query filters `deleted_at === null`; this one is missing that check.

### 2. `totalPaidCents counts only paid orders` (`tests/order-service.test.js`)
`src/services/order-service.js:9` filters on `o.status === 'quote'` when it should filter on `'paid'`. It returns 1350, which is the single quote order, instead of 14600 (4200 + 9900 + 500).

### 3. `uncapturedTotalCents sums uncaptured payments` (`tests/payment-service.test.js`)
`src/services/payment-service.js:10` filters on `p.captured === true`, the opposite of what the function's name says. It returns 4200, the captured payment, instead of 9900, the uncaptured one.

### Why the failure messages are confusing
The test output nests one assertion error inside another, for example `+ AssertionError ... 1350 !== 14600` reported as the *actual* value with `- null` as *expected*. That comes from `query()` in `src/db.js:33-36`. It wraps the callback in `try/catch`, so when a test's assertion throws inside the callback, `db.js` catches it and calls the callback a second time with that error as `err`. The test's first check, `assert.equal(err, null)`, then fails on the second call. The real failure is the inner error (e.g. `1350 !== 14600`). This doesn't cause any of the failures, but it makes them harder to read: any assertion that fails inside a `query` callback will show up as an error being called back twice.
